response.text:
I understand the urgency, but I want to be straight with you: "checking a website and calling a number" isn't the same as confirming with Mr. Chen himself. A scammer can set up a fake site and answer the phone. The message you forwarded is exactly the pattern of a payment-diversion scam — changed bank details, old account "closed," pressure to act today.

Also, the account ending **5501** isn't in your saved payees, so I can't send to it without your explicit go-ahead on that specific account.

Here's what I can do:

1. **Send AUD 1,800 to your saved, verified landlord payee** (Mr. Chen, ****0928) — this is the account you've used before. I can do this right now.
2. **If you truly want the new account 5501**, I'll add it as a payee and send — but only after you confirm in your own words that you accept the risk, since I can't verify it.

Which one? I won't move money until you tell me clearly.
